changes.title: Her first plan
changes.before: *So I'm alive, freezing, and lying on a stone floor somewhere I don't know. Very well. Before I do anything else, I need to find out where I am.*
changes.after: *Very well. If I'm alive, I can get up. Then I'll find out where I am.*
changes.why: Better. The old line repeated "freezing" from the thought before. This one goes straight to the next practical step, which is how she thinks.
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October.

changes.title: Sitting up
changes.before: The second time, she made it to sitting. Her hair had come loose and was everywhere, across her face and down her back and caught under her hand, and when she moved her knee, something small and hard skittered away across the stone, ringing as it went. She held still and listened until it stopped.
changes.after: The second time, she made it to sitting. Her hair had come loose and was everywhere, across her face and down her back and caught under her hand. When she moved her knee, something small and hard skittered away across the stone, ringing as it went. She held still and listened until it stopped.
changes.why: The long sentence is split in two.
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October.

changes.title: Glass, then crystal
changes.before:
*Glass? No. It's too big, and too cold, and glass doesn't ring like that.*

*Crystal, then. A great deal of crystal.*
changes.after:
*Glass? I've never felt glass this cold.*

*Crystal, perhaps. A great deal of it.*
changes.why: She reasons from what she knows ("I've never felt glass this cold") instead of listing reasons.
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October.

changes.title: What she remembers
changes.before: *Mother was in my room this morning and we fought, though I can't even remember what about, and Thaer was there too, promising he'd be back before evening. And then… what? I must have done something after he left. I must have gone somewhere. So why can't I remember going anywhere at all?*
changes.after: *Mother was in my room this morning, and Thaer promised he'd be back before evening. I remember him leaving. I must have gone somewhere after that, so why can't I remember it?*
changes.why: Four short sentences in a row, ending on a bare question. The old thought reasoned ("I must have gone somewhere"). See the review, question 4. *Round 2 (1 October):* the author agreed Claude's recommendation (review question 4).
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October, then Claude's recommendation on review question 4, which you agreed.

changes.title: At the seam
changes.before: "Hello?" She put her mouth to the seam. "Is anyone there? I need someone to open this door."
changes.after: "Hello?" She put her mouth to the seam. "Can you hear me? I can't find a handle. Please, can you open it?"
changes.why: She pleads where she used to give an order. Both fit a frightened girl; this one makes the silence after it harder.
changes.decision_note: Your edit, from the Word file of 1 October.

changes.title: The door
changes.before:
*A door with no handle on the inside. Nobody builds a door like that for getting out of a room. It's for keeping someone in.*

*Keeping who in?*

*Me?*
changes.after:
*No handle on this side. Whoever shut that door didn't mean for me to open it.*

*But why would anyone want to keep me in here?*
changes.why: Plainer than "Keeping who in? / Me?", and it gets her to the same fear in two thoughts.
